content:
· Results-Based Financing (RBF): The implementation of the project, particularly acknowledging the fragile context in CAR, will link the disbursement of funds to achievement of adaptation milestones (e.g., hectares restored, livestock vaccinated). This approach will encourage performance and accountability while mitigating financial risk for implementing partners.
· Piloting green livelihood enterprises and market access: The project will also support youth- and women-led enterprises involving solar-powered boreholes and charging stations, but also veterinary services. De-risking will involve startup capital, business mentoring, or subsidized equipment with climate co-benefits. The project will support infrastructure and value chains such as climate-proof livestock markets that reduce volatility and increase returns. In this regard, the project will finance digital platforms to connect producers to markets and provide real- time pricing, thus lowering income uncertainty. In sum, access to markets transforms smallholders from subsistence actors into active, bankable economic agents, making climate and financial risks more manageable for all stakeholders in the crop and livestock agricultural ecosystem.

content:
· Paraguay has special tax exemptions that can benefit industries along EVs' value chain. Under the Law No. 60/90, there are tax exemption benefits to foreign and local investors for inputs for local industry for the fabrication of capital goods. The Maquila Regime, under the Law No. 1064/97, allows investors to "import goods or products to be assembled, repaired, improved, worked on, or processed with the purpose of exporting such goods or products, prior to the addition of value or the 'Paraguayan component'. This regime is subject to a special tax treatment: a 1% tax rate applies to the value added within Paraguayan territory"15. The Free Trade Zone regime, under the Law No. 523/95 and its regulatory decree No. 15, 554/96 allows for the development of industrial, commercial and service activities with advantageous tax exemptions. There are two trade zones in Paraguay-both are located in the Alto Parana Department near the border with Brazil and Argentina.
· Paraguay's proximity to Bolivia also poses a potential benefit for making it a hub of EVs' value chain. Bolivia has approximately 52% of the world's lithium brines reserves16 - a key element for EV vehicle batteries.

note: 10-K commodity-hedging prose
content: The derivative commodity instruments we use are primarily swap, collar and option agreements. note: soils prose with (Lal, 2016) parentheticals - must be KEPT
content: According to the World Reference Base (WRB) classification for soil resources, Seychellois soils consist of Arenosols (Coastal Sandy Soil), Ferralsols (Red Ferralitic Soil) and Colluvial Soil, with the main cultivated soils being the Arenosol and the Ferralsol soils. These two soil types are relatively poor in soil organic matter (OM), organic carbon (OC) and cation exchange capacity (CEC) (Nourice, 2020). Soil degradation across the islands is however occurring as a consequence of a range of chemical, biological or physical factors (Qadir and Schubert, 2002, Diop et al., 2022). These processes of degradation have high intractability and can cause significant losses of soil biodiversity (Lal, 2016). However, all three processes of degradation are all highly dependent on the amount of organic matter and organic carbon that is present within the soil (Lal, 2015). There are two main ways by which organic matter and organic carbon integrate into the soil strata.

note: biodiversity prose with (Carr et al. 2015) parentheticals - must be KEPT
content: WWF designated the Western Guinean Lowland Forest ecoregion and two regions of the Lower Guinean forests (Coastal Congolian Forests and Cameroon Highlands forests) as Global 200 priority regions for conservation (Olson and Dinnerstein 2002). The GFB has high levels of both species richness and endemism. The region is home to over 9,000 species of vascular plants, of which more than 1,800 are endemic (Mittermeier et al. 2004). Its over 416 mammal species represent a quarter of all native African species, with approximately 65 species categorized as endemic to the region. Other terrestrial taxa include 917 birds, 107 reptiles and 269 amphibian species, of which 48 birds, 20 reptiles and 118 amphibians are endemic (Carr et al. 2015). Freshwater ecosystems in the region also have high levels of diversity, with approximately one-third of the freshwater fish species thought to be endemic to the GFB (Paugy et al. 2003).

note: AfDB mini-grid programme prose
content: The AfDB is currently the focal point for all mini-grid activities on the continent. Through its Green Mini-Grids Market Development Programme (GMG MDP), the Bank offers technical assistance to mini-grid developers and mini-grid policy makers through its GMG Help Desk (http://greenminigrid.se4all-africa.org). We are currently providing support to more than 60 GMG developers in 30 countries, as well as to several Ministries of Energy. The GMG MDP drafted the GMG Africa Strategy, which was endorsed in 2017 by the African Union Commission. The GMG Africa Strategy is a document that prescribes the baseline policy principles required to foster private sector investment into mini-grids development in a particular country.
